name: Herbal Remedies for Menorrhagia (Heavy Menstrual Bleeding)

sections.herbal_remedies:
About Menorrhagia 
 Menorrhagia refers to heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding and is classified as a type of abnormal uterine bleeding. This is different from normal periods as in this a person cannot continue daily activities due to severe blood loss and cramps. 
 In the process of menstrual cycle, there is a loss of blood every 28-35 days from the uterus due to expulsion of the inner lining of the uterus known as Endometrium. This process sets off at puberty in females and continues till menopause in the mid-40s to 50s. 
 Factors that affect the menstrual cycle include diet, hormonal changes, lifestyle, sleep patterns, and underlying health issues. These factors also impact overall body health. 
 The normal blood flow during the menstrual cycle is 30-40 ml per cycle and if this increases, it reaches to 60-80 ml per cycle. This results in heavy bleeding which give rise to the condition known as Menorrhagia.
sections.causes_of_menorrhagia:
Hormonal imbalance: There are two main hormones that regulates the functioning of the reproductive system namely Estrogen and Progesterone. These two hormones build up the lining of uterus and that lining is shed during the menstruation cycle. The imbalance in the hormones may lead to excessive development of endometrium. 
 Ovary dysfunction: Sometimes, the ovary does not ovulate and the body does not produce the hormone progesterone. This may also lead to Menorrhagia. 
 Uterine fibroids: During the child bearing year, uterine fibroids may occur causing heavy and prolonged bleeding during menstruation cycle. 
 Polyps: These are the small growths on the lining of uterus that may cause heavy bleeding. 
 Adenomyosis: In this the tissue of endometrium become embedded in the uterine muscle that cause heavy bleeding and painful periods. 
 Intrauterine device: This is a birth control device and is considered as a major cause of Pregnancy complications.
sections.symptoms_of_menorrhagia:
Heavy menstrual bleeding 
 Needing to use double sanitary protection 
 Waking up at night to change sanitary protection 
 Menstrual periods lasting longer than 7 days 
 Passing large blood clots 
 Feeling tired, fatigued, or short of breath 
 Restricted daily activities due to heavy menstrual flow 




 Prolonged and excessive bleeding 
 Abdominal cramps
sections.diagnosis_of_menorrhagia:
Evaluation of the cervical infection 
 Ultrasound can be done to evaluate pelvis organs including the uterus, ovaries and pelvis. 
 A fluid is inserted into the uterus to evaluate the uterus for abnormalities. This is called a sonohysterogram.
